data.title: Corrected validity estimates place structured interviews above general mental ability
data.summary: Sackett et al. (2022) found that the standard corrections for range restriction had systematically overstated the criterion-related validity of several selection methods, and re-estimated them. As reported in this paper's side-by-side table, the earlier Roth et al. (2011) values for biodata, general mental ability tests, conscientiousness tests, structured interviews and integrity tests were .32, .52, .22, .48 and .42; the corrected values are .38, .31, .19, .42 and .31. Structured interviews therefore become the strongest single predictor of job performance in that set, ahead of general mental ability. These are validity coefficients for predicting performance once hired; nothing here measures whether a scoring scheme is applied consistently or published in advance.
data.citation: Berry, C. M., Lievens, F., Zhang, C., & Sackett, P. R. Insights from an Updated Personnel Selection Meta-analytic Matrix: Revisiting General Mental Ability Tests' Role in the Validity-Diversity Tradeoff. Reporting corrected estimates from Sackett, P. R., Zhang, C., Berry, C. M., & Lievens, F. (2022), Journal of Applied Psychology.
